unusual_experiment.name: JCS_BINARY64_V8_DIFFERENTIAL_50014
unusual_experiment.purpose: falsify the selected HCU JCS float serializer by comparing its exact binary64 canonical text against an independent V8 JSON.stringify oracle over deterministic edge cases plus random finite IEEE-754 bit patterns

interpretation.supported: For the tested finite binary64 corpus, the exact PR1263 JCS candidate float serializer matched V8 JSON number serialization byte-for-byte.
interpretation.known_adjacent_counterevidence: PR1378 separately identifies Python-int versus binary64 host-type inconsistency in this candidate and proposes a repair; this experiment does not retire that defect.
interpretation.historical_triangulation: The 2026-08-09 ClayCode numeric run showed host-native Python-vs-Node JSON presentation mismatches; this experiment tests the newer explicit HCU JCS candidate rather than host-native Python JSON and observed zero mismatches on the bounded corpus.

artefact_readme.reason: Current README already states the single-versioned canonicalization convergence gate and exact combined Entry+route+inference+GRID10 execution blocker; this bounded float differential does not change product-facing acceptance language.

next_discriminator: Resolve the PR1378 host-int repair and single canonicalizer selection, then run exact combined Typed Entry + route + inference receipt + GRID10 regressions on an actually-started authorized isolated executor before any HCU runtime promotion.
